title: Search query sequences against a target sequence database

sources.locator: Getting started > Search; supported search modes; memory requirements
workflow stages: createdb, selected search module, convertalis, optional taxonomyreport

scientific_use: Find homologous or similar target sequences for query proteins or nucleotides; return tabular alignments with configurable columns. Repeated searches can reuse a precomputed target index.
tool_role_basis: README demonstrates invoking MMseqs2 workflows; easysearch.sh composes existing createdb, search, convertalis and optional taxonomyreport commands.
inputs: Query and target FASTA/FASTQ files or MMseqs2 sequence databases; README demo uses examples/QUERY.fasta and examples/DB.fasta, linked as mmseqs2_examples_query_fasta and mmseqs2_examples_db_fasta.
Optional indexed or padded target DB and search/sensitivity/output-format parameters.
outputs: Alignment result in user-selected tabular format (example .m8); optional taxonomy report when target is taxonomically annotated.
dependencies: MMseqs2 binary and temporary directory; substantial CPU, memory and disk depend on database size; optional prebuilt index or GPU build/device for GPU mode.
evidence: README Search example explicitly uses QUERY.fasta against DB.fasta and documents index reuse, GPU option and format output.
easysearch.sh stages DB creation, search and convertalis.
limitations: No exact biological identity or reference labels for bundled FASTA fixtures were inspected.
Search sensitivity, real identity reporting and output fields require explicit choices; default search identity may be estimated.
No execution or deterministic grading behavior assessed.

title: Cluster protein or nucleotide sequence sets

sources.locator: Getting started > Cluster; memory requirements
createdb, cluster module, createtsv, representative sequence export
linear-time clustering workflow stages
redundancy precluster, cluster1 multi-step or cluster2 representative-based branch, optional reassignment and representative switch
redundancy reduction, frame extraction, alignment, clustering and merge

sources.revision: mutable wiki page, last edited 2026-09-07; fetched 2026-09-30
sources.locator: Writing large scale sequence analysis workflows > Redundancy reduction

scientific_use: Group related sequences by similarity to reduce redundancy or define sequence families, with representative sequences and member-to-cluster assignments. Default easy-cluster uses cascaded clustering; easy-linclust is presented for very large sets with runtime scaling linearly in input size. The cascaded workflow first reduces redundancy, then offers multi-step cluster1 or representative-based cluster2; optional branches reassign sequences or choose a consensus representative. A separate nucleotide workflow handles translated nucleotide comparisons.
tool_role_basis: The sources compose MMseqs2 clustering, alignment and database commands; the inventory records use of the existing algorithms, not implementation changes.
inputs: FASTA/FASTQ sequence collection; README example uses examples/DB.fasta. Thresholds such as minimum sequence identity and coverage are user-selected.
For nucleotide_clustering workflow, sequence DB plus configured ORF/frame and alignment parameters.
outputs: Cluster membership TSV and representative-sequence FASTA in easy workflow; internal cluster DB in lower-level workflows.
dependencies: MMseqs2 binary; temporary storage and memory roughly proportional to sequence residues per README; clustering criteria and workflow parameters affect result. Cascaded branch and optional reassignment/representative selection are configured separately.
evidence: README Cluster gives easy-cluster command with min-seq-id and coverage and names easy-linclust for huge datasets.
easycluster.sh creates input DB, invokes cluster module, exports cluster.tsv and representative sequences.
cascaded_clustering.sh branches on cluster1/cluster2, with optional reassignment and consensus representative selection.
nucleotide_clustering.sh shows redundancy clustering, frame extraction, prefilter/alignment, cluster and merge stages.
Tutorial applies easy-cluster at 90% identity and 95% coverage to Plass proteins assembled from ERR1384114 paired metagenomic reads.
limitations: Example FASTA contents and biological provenance unknown.
Cluster semantics depend on coverage mode, identity threshold, sensitivity and selected algorithm; exact criteria need task specification.
Memory and runtime can be large; no execution was performed.

title: Assign taxonomy to query sequences and report taxa

sources.locator: Getting started > Taxonomy
taxonomy, LCA TSV, taxonomy report and top-hit alignment report stages
ORF extraction/filtering, taxonomy and contig-level taxonomic aggregation

sources.revision: mutable wiki page, last edited 2026-09-07; fetched 2026-09-30
sources.locator: Contig taxonomic assignment and auxiliary modules > download Swiss-Prot, taxonomy command, sample assignment report

scientific_use: Assign query sequences a taxon using a taxonomy-annotated sequence DB, selected aligned hits and an LCA mode; produce per-query taxonomic assignments and summary reports. Taxpercontig projects ORF-level classifications back to contigs with aggregatetaxweights.
tool_role_basis: The workflows orchestrate existing taxonomy, alignment, reporting and aggregation commands. No underlying algorithm implementation is modified by the documented use.
inputs: Query sequences; target sequence DB with taxonomy mappings. README describes createtaxdb for UniProt accessions/NCBI taxonomy and notes BLAST, SILVA or custom sources are supported.
For taxpercontig: contig DB and taxonomy sequence DB; ORFs are extracted and optionally filtered before classification.
outputs: Per-query LCA TSV, taxonomy summary report, top-hit report/alignment; taxpercontig can emit contig tax assignments and/or alignment outputs according to TAX_OUTPUT.
dependencies: MMseqs2; taxonomy-aware target DB and compatible taxonomy mapping/tree; temporary directory. Reference acquisition/setup is separate and may require network and substantial storage.
evidence: README explains representative aligned target selection by --lca-mode and taxonomy DB preparation.
easytaxonomy.sh calls taxonomy, createtsv, taxonomyreport and top-hit reporting stages.
taxpercontig.sh extracts ORFs and aggregates their taxonomy weights to contigs.
Tutorial supplies Swiss-Prot 2018-03 protein FASTA/mapping and a contig taxonomy example with reported Saccharomyces cerevisiae assignment; the page is mutable.
limitations: No specific taxonomic reference DB was inspected or registered as a dataset; the README's demo sequence DB is not shown as taxonomy annotated.
Taxonomic correctness depends on reference snapshot, mapping completeness, LCA mode and search parameters.
No task outputs were executed or validated.

title: Search nucleotide sequences through translated reading frames

sources.locator: Supported search modes > Translated searches
query/target ORF extraction, delegated search, offsetalignment

scientific_use: Search nucleotide sequences in translated reading frames against protein sequences, or other translated query/target combinations (blastx, tblastn, tblastx), then map protein-space alignments back to nucleotide coordinates.
tool_role_basis: translated_search.sh composes existing ORF extraction, search and offsetalignment modules; it does not implement a new algorithm.
inputs: Nucleotide and/or protein sequence DBs; flags determine which side is nucleotide and whether ORFs are extracted or frames enumerated.
outputs: Alignment DB with offsets restored to original nucleotide sequence coordinates.
dependencies: MMseqs2 and selected search workflow; nucleotide translation/frame policy and optional ORF filtering/indexing affect coordinates and results.
evidence: README enumerates nucleotide-protein, protein-nucleotide and nucleotide-nucleotide translated modes.
translated_search.sh extracts ORFs or frames as configured and calls offsetalignment to map results back.
limitations: No nucleotide/protein dataset with identified study provenance was inspected.
Genetic code, ORF policy and actual search module configuration require resolution for a task.
No run or coordinate correctness check was performed.

title: Identify reciprocal best hit sequence pairs

sources.locator: Supported search modes > Reciprocal best hits search
bidirectional searches, best-hit filtering, result swapping, merge and result2rbh
FASTA conversion, optional GPU padding, RBH and tabular export

scientific_use: Compare two sequence collections in both directions and identify pairs that are each other's best hit, a candidate orthology-related result requiring biological interpretation.
tool_role_basis: Workflow calls existing search/filter/swap/merge/result2rbh commands and formats results.
inputs: Two sequence collections A and B as MMseqs2 DBs or FASTA/FASTQ through easy-rbh; search parameters determine best-hit selection.
outputs: RBH pair result DB or converted tabular alignments.
dependencies: MMseqs2; both search directions, matching sequence identifiers, adequate temporary disk; optional GPU-compatible build and padded DB.
evidence: rbh.sh searches A vs B and B vs A, selects best hits in each direction, swaps/merges and calls result2rbh.
easyrbh.sh exposes the workflow for FASTA inputs and converts result alignments.
limitations: No specific paired species/proteome datasets were identified; biological orthology is not established by RBH alone.
Tie handling, thresholds and sequence coverage need task-level decisions.
Source review only; no search was run.

title: Iterative sequence-to-profile search

sources.locator: Supported search modes > Iterative sequences-profile searches
iteration loop: search, profile consensus, prefilter, align, expand profile/alignment

inputs: Query sequence DB, target sequence DB and target alignment/sequence artifacts expected by workflow; number of iterations and per-step parameters.

evidence: README identifies iterative sequence-profile search as a supported mode.
iterativepp.sh derives consensus, repeatedly prefilters and aligns, then expands alignments or profiles.
limitations: Workflow expects hidden target companion DBs and a specific preparation not completely documented in the inspected script.
Profile convergence, iteration count, false-positive control and final result interpretation require task design.

title: Cluster protein sequences and summarize relationships among proteomes

sources.locator: protein clusters, proteomecluster, cluster counts and optional cascade
sequence search followed by parseproteomealignments and score TSV

scientific_use: From sequences associated with proteomes, cluster protein sequences, map/aggregate cluster relationships at proteome level and report cluster counts; related easy-proteome-search parses sequence alignments into a proteome-level score table.
tool_role_basis: The workflows call existing clustering, search, proteomecluster, parseproteomealignments and TSV conversion commands.
inputs: Protein FASTA/FASTQ entries with source-to-proteome membership metadata expected by proteomecluster workflow; easyproteomesearch needs query and target sequences with compatible proteome source metadata.
outputs: Protein cluster membership TSV, proteome cluster/alignment TSVs and cluster-count TSV; proteome search emits sequence alignment M8 and proteome-level score TSV.
dependencies: MMseqs2; source and lookup metadata (`input.source`, `input.lookup`) retained/created in the database; cascading mode may iterate over residual proteomes.
evidence: easyproteomecluster.sh invokes a protein clustering module, then proteomecluster and exports cluster counts and proteome groupings.
easyproteomesearch.sh invokes search, convertalis, parseproteomealignments and exports scores.
limitations: The inspected scripts reveal hidden membership metadata dependencies but do not document the biological meaning/format or prepare the supplied source metadata.
No reference proteomes or scientific study dataset identified.
Whether proteome search and proteome clustering warrant separate tasks is author decision; kept together here as related outputs from the paired workflow family.

title: Aggregate sequence hits by set and retain best hit per target set

sources.locator: nucleotide DB conversion, contig-to-set and ORF/member-to-set mappings, set sizes
search, besthitperset and mergeresultsbyset

scientific_use: For nucleotide sequence collections grouped into sets, translate contig ORFs, establish member-to-set mappings and set sizes, search sequences, retain the best hit per target set, then merge per-set results. This can compare query groups to target groups while accounting for set-level membership.
tool_role_basis: The paired workflows compose createdb, ORF translation, mapping conversion, search, besthitperset and mergeresultsbyset commands.
inputs: Nucleotide FASTA entries with third-column set identifiers in the generated database lookup metadata; query and target databases must carry compatible set mapping artifacts.
outputs: Set-level best-hit alignments and set-size/membership mapping databases.
dependencies: MMseqs2; `multihitdb.sh` only implements nucleotide mode, derives set IDs from lookup field 3, and produces `_set_to_member`, `_member_to_set` and `_set_size` artifacts required by search.
evidence: multihitdb.sh extracts set IDs from lookup metadata, extracts/translates ORFs and builds member/set mappings and set sizes.
multihitsearch.sh searches and uses besthitperset then mergeresultsbyset.
limitations: Biological definition of sets is supplied through input identifiers and is not established by the tool.
The script's entry-level parameter contract and required naming conventions need author confirmation.
No sample set/grouped dataset was identified or processed.

title: Update existing sequence clusters after sequence collection changes

sources.locator: old/new sequence diff and key mapping, removed-member handling, search new sequences against old representatives, cluster unmatched sequences

scientific_use: Maintain a prior clustering when a new sequence database adds/removes/retains entries: map common keys, handle removed members, assign new sequences to old representatives where possible, separately cluster unmatched sequences, and emit updated clustering plus mapped sequence DB.
tool_role_basis: The script composes existing database diff, key remapping, representative extraction, search, filtering, clustering and merge commands.
inputs: Old and new sequence DBs, old cluster DB, output mapped sequence DB and output cluster DB; optional policy to recover deleted sequences.
outputs: Updated key-mapped sequence DB and updated cluster DB, with new sequences either merged into existing representative groups or newly clustered.
dependencies: MMseqs2; sequence IDs and DB keys must be comparable across versions; search and clustering thresholds and removed-sequence policy affect assignments.
evidence: update_clustering.sh declares six input/output artifacts, detects common/removed/new sequences, searches new sequences against prior representatives and clusters no-hit sequences separately.
limitations: A realistic task needs versioned old/new DBs and a prior clustering oracle; none is supplied in inspected sources.
Deleted-sequence recovery changes whether historical entries remain in the output and needs explicit decision.

title: Use translated homology and taxonomy evidence to investigate a metagenomic pathogen

sources.revision: mutable wiki page, last edited 2026-09-07; fetched 2026-09-30
sources.locator: Investigating the pathogen; filtertaxdb, read extraction, Plass assembly, easy-cluster and domain annotation steps

scientific_use: Analyze a published encephalitis case from host-filtered CSF metagenomic reads: assign taxonomy by translated homology to annotated Swiss-Prot, summarize assignments, inspect alternative taxa, filter candidate-pathogen reads, assemble candidate proteins with Plass, cluster representatives with MMseqs2 and annotate against protein/domain references. The task question includes identifying likely pathogen and evaluating support, not only running a command.
tool_role_basis: Tutorial composes existing MMseqs2 taxonomy/filter/cluster operations with Plass assembly, Kraken preprocessing context and manual literature interpretation; it does not implement the underlying algorithms.
inputs: Tutorial-linked mystery_reads.fasta (226,908 human-filtered CSF reads, derived from 14 million reads); curated UniProt Swiss-Prot sequence and taxonomic mapping files labelled 2018-03; taxonomic labels and human-readable patient case context.
outputs: Per-read taxon assignments and summary report; pathogen-filtered read FASTA; Plass protein assemblies; MMseqs2 clusters/representatives; follow-up candidate protein annotations.
dependencies: MMseqs2, Plass, tutorial environment; Swiss-Prot plus mapping and NCBI taxonomy setup; NCBI taxon IDs and external protein-domain search; scientific interpretation and cited clinical paper.
evidence: Tutorial reports CSF metagenomic sequencing on day 8, 14 million reads, and released 226,908 human-depleted reads; directs translation/search against Swiss-Prot and taxonomy reporting.
Tutorial gives MMseqs2 taxonomy commands and questions about most common species, plausible pathogens and read support.
Tutorial then filters taxon reads, assembles with Plass, clusters assembled proteins using easy-cluster and recommends domain annotation against PFAM/PDB/Uniclust.
limitations: Wiki is mutable; the fetched page says last edited 2026-09-07, not an immutable revision.
